balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For The Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For The Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For The Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; Diluted EPS additionally assumes conversion of outstanding options/awards into shares; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. All are in HKD major units.

For The Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested; Towngas has held DPS roughly flat through 2022-2025 while EPS recovered off the FY2021-22 energy-cost shock, so payout ratio has been falling from an elevated level rather than the dividend being cut.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Basic vs diluted EPS gap widening (more dilutive awards outstanding)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

customers.title: Customer base: Hong Kong vs mainland city-gas
customers.content:
HK customers is the metered town-gas customer count in Hong Kong (thousands); mainland city-gas customers is the combined customer count across Towngas's mainland China city-gas joint ventures (thousands) -- roughly 20x the HK base.

For The Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited: HK is a mature, near-saturated franchise growing low-single-digit on new housing connections; the mainland JVs are the growth engine, adding well over a million customers a year as city-gas penetration deepens. Only FY2023-FY2025 are extracted here -- earlier years appeared only as chart images in the annual reports, not as parseable text.

What to watch:

  • Mainland customer growth rate decelerating as penetration matures
  • HK customer count against HK population/household trends (little room left to grow)

gasSold.title: Gas sold: HK town gas vs mainland natural gas
gasSold.content:
HK town gas sold (million MJ) is metered on a calorific-value basis, the traditional HK town-gas convention. Mainland gas sold (million m3) is natural gas sold by the mainland city-gas JVs, measured volumetrically -- the two are not the same unit and are not directly comparable on one axis.

For The Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited: HK volume has been essentially flat (~27,100-27,200 million MJ across FY2023-FY2025) -- a mature franchise paying out cash rather than growing -- while mainland volume is roughly flat too over the two years it is disclosed (FY2024-FY2025), consistent with China's slower post-pandemic gas-demand growth and JV disposals/dilutions in the mainland portfolio.

What to watch:

  • HK volume growth (or lack of it) versus the customer count above -- flat volume per customer means no usage growth, just new connections
  • Mainland volume growth against China's city-gas sector demand trends and any JV stake changes

hkHeadcount.title: Hong Kong company employees
hkHeadcount.content:
HK company employees is headcount for the Hong Kong town-gas operating company only -- it excludes mainland JV staff, who are employed by the separately-managed joint ventures.

For The Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited: a labour-productivity check for the mature HK business: compare against HK customers and HK gas sold above to see whether the HK operation is getting more efficient per employee as volumes stay flat.

What to watch:

  • Headcount growing while HK customers/volume stay flat (productivity declining)
  • Only FY2023-FY2025 disclosed; not comparable to any mainland headcount figure

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For The Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For The Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For The Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For The Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For The Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For The Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
